title: What Did Review Require?
question: Was the 1902 review adequate to the identity and ancestry question it actually decided?
standing: working research-through-design specimen; source descriptions are bounded and do not decide identity, entitlement, or administrative failure
brakes: EXISTED ≠ IN CASE ≠ NAMED IN REVIEW ≠ REQUIRED TO CONSULT ≠ ADEQUATE / INADEQUATE
Catherine ≠ Catharine until an independently controlled identity bridge is earned
A bounded absence from the stated review text does not prove no consultation elsewhere
Potential relevance plus an unnamed carrier does not prove administrative failure
A visitor-supplied ticket is not a verified source

review.title: The transmitted MCR 879 case record
review.text: On 19 April 1902 the Commission transmitted the consolidated record and its decision to the Secretary, through Indian Affairs.
review.brake: Transmitted case record ≠ every federal record relevant to the people named in it.

review.title: Commission McKinney surname-record negative
review.text: The Commission decision carries a bounded negative concerning persons named McKinney in a specified compliance / Ward / later-commission record frame.
review.brake: Surname-wide negative in named record domains ≠ search of every McKinney treaty-land record population.

meta.verb: reports no showing in named frame
meta.source: p.-57 governing jacket / OHC decision body

review.title: Indian Affairs adds its own Robert records
review.text: The 13 May review uses the case record plus Office-held material including Record Book No. 102, a Robert Bell patent record, and an Office-held Mississippi map.
review.brake: Named Office additions establish documentary reach, not an exhaustive inventory of everything available to the Office.

review.title: Interior says it reviewed the whole case
review.text: On 4 June Interior says that after a careful review of the whole case it approves the Commission action and affirms the decision.
review.brake: “Whole case” proves the Department’s characterization of its review object; it does not by itself define every external federal record it was obliged to search.

other.title: Family names Catherine McKinney
other.text: Sarah Carroll’s 29 April 1901 examination names Catherine McKinney as her father’s grandmother, then names her father Robert Bell.
other.brake: Family Catherine ≠ Public Lands Catharine until independently bridged.

other.title: 1831 Public Lands Catharine McKinney
other.text: The farm-return body carries Catharine McKinney with 40 cultivated acres, family six, a Yazoo Valley locality chain, and 480 total acres.
other.brake: Farm-return occurrence ≠ patent occurrence; spelling remains Catharine.

other.title: Article XIX three-quarter class
other.text: Forty cultivated acres falls in Article XIX’s 30-to-under-50-acre class, nominally three quarter sections / 480 acres.
other.brake: Treaty-class fit ≠ final adjudication or person identity.

other.title: Separate Catharine Article XIX patent path
other.text: A later patent face recites three-quarter Article XIX entitlement, Sec. 11 T17N R1E, sale to Linsey C. Hall, presidential approval, and 1850 patent to Hall.
other.brake: Patent recital ≠ underlying deed / approval record; patent-path Catharine ≠ farm-return Catharine without a bridge.

other.title: Reserve File C — Article XIX case architecture
other.text: RG 75 preserves a distinct Article XIX case system with index, register, correspondence, reports, legal documents, maps, plats, disposal and inheritance material.
other.brake: Archive-series existence ≠ Catharine case recovered ≠ 1902 consultation.

other.title: Federal sale-certification branch
other.text: Separate federal records preserve Brown/Kincannon reports concerning certification of Choctaw reserve sales; the controlled printed Brown extract carries a Catharine McKinney sale occurrence.
other.brake: Sales-report occurrence still needs exact cross-carrier identity and MCR 879 carriage testing.

meta.object: reports concerning certification of land sales
meta.source: PI 163 entry 263 + controlled printed Brown extract

open: Catherine and Catharine remain separate until a source-grounded identity bridge is earned.
Article XIX carriage into the transmitted MCR 879 case remains open.
The full documentary reach required of the 1902 substantive reviewers remains open.
PROVED ADMINISTRATIVE FAILURE is not yet earned.
